classification.difficultyReason: The assumption is rearranged to 7^k=6p-5 and substituted, as in the reference.

content.prompt: $7^n+5$ is divisible by $6$ for all integers $n\geq1$.

answer.short: $7^{k+1}+5=6(7p-5)$, using $7^k+5=6p$. The base case is true, so the result holds for every integer $n\geq1$ by induction.
answer.worked:
Test $n=1$
$$\mathrm{LHS}=7^1+5=12=6(2)$$
$\therefore$ True for $n=1$

Assume true for $n=k$
$7^k+5=6p$, where $p$ is an integer.

Prove $n=k+1$
WTP: $7^{k+1}+5=6q$, where $q$ is an integer.
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{LHS}&=7^{k+1}+5\\&=7\times7^k+5\\&=7(6p-5)+5\quad\text{using assumption}\\&=42p-35+5\\&=42p-30\\&=6(7p-5)\\&=6q\end{align*}$$
Since $p$ is an integer, $q=7p-5$ is also an integer.

Since the statement is true for $n=1$ and truth for $n=k$ implies truth for $n=k+1$, it is true for all integers $n\geq1$ by mathematical induction.
